back: The phenomenon in which electric current is generated by varying magnetic fields. Discovered by Faraday (England) and Henry (USA) around 1830.

Pushing/pulling a bar magnet near a coil induces current only while the magnet is in motion. Faster motion gives larger deflection. Reversing the pole or direction reverses the current. Relative motion matters.
Moving a current-carrying coil C2 towards/away from coil C1 induces current in C1 - the steady field of C2 must change through C1. Again relative motion induces the current.

Two stationary coils; pressing/releasing a tapping key K in the C2 circuit induces a momentary current in C1. Relative motion is not an absolute requirement - a changing field suffices. An iron rod core amplifies the effect.
Phi_B = B . A = BA cos(theta), where theta is the angle between B and the area vector A. SI unit: weber (Wb) or T m^2. Scalar. General: Phi_B = sum B_i . dA_i.
The magnitude of the induced emf equals the time rate of change of magnetic flux: epsilon = -d(Phi_B)/dt. For N turns: epsilon = -N d(Phi_B)/dt. The negative sign gives the direction of the emf.
Change B, change A (shape), or change theta (angle between B and A) - e.g., rotating a coil in a field, or shrinking/stretching a coil.
The polarity of the induced emf is such that it tends to produce a current which opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. The negative sign in Faraday's law represents this.

front: Lenz's law and conservation of energy
back: If induced current assisted the change, a gentle push would give perpetual motion (ever-increasing KE without work). In reality the magnet is repelled/attracted to oppose the change, and the work done appears as Joule heat.

epsilon = Blv, for a conductor of length l moving with speed v perpendicular to a uniform field B. Obtained from Faraday's law (rate of change of enclosed flux) or the Lorentz force (work qvBl per charge).

front: Stationary conductor in changing magnetic field
back: With v = 0, F = q(E + v x B) = qE - the force must come from an electric field. Hence a time-varying magnetic field generates an electric field. This is the fundamental significance of Faraday's discovery.
Flux linkage N.Phi_B is proportional to current I. Inductance L = N.Phi_B/I. Scalar, dimensions [M L^2 T^-2 A^-2], SI unit henry (H). Depends on geometry and material properties.
N1.Phi1 = M12 . I2 defines mutual inductance of coil 1 wrt coil 2. General equality: M12 = M21 = M. Depends on separation and relative orientation of the two coils.
M = mu_0 n1 n2 pi r1^2 l (inner solenoid radius r1). With a medium of relative permeability mu_r: M = mu_r mu_0 n1 n2 pi r1^2 l.

front: Mutual inductance of concentric circular coils
back: For r1 << r2 co-centric coils, M = mu_0 pi r1^2 / (2 r2). Field of the outer coil is uniform over the small inner coil.
epsilon = -L dI/dt. The self-induced emf always opposes any change (increase or decrease) of current in the coil - L is the electrical analogue of inertia/mass.
L = mu_0 n^2 A l (area A, length l, n turns/unit length). With a core of relative permeability mu_r: L = mu_r mu_0 n^2 A l.
W = (1/2) L I^2. Work done against the back emf to build up current I, stored as magnetic potential energy. Analogue of kinetic energy (1/2)m v^2.
u_B = (1/2) B^2 / mu_0, analogous to electrostatic u_E = (1/2)epsilon_0 E^2. Both valid generally, energy proportional to square of field strength.
Flux Phi_B = BA cos(omega t); emf epsilon = -N d(Phi_B)/dt = NBA omega sin(omega t) = epsilon_0 sin(omega t) = epsilon_0 sin(2 pi n t). Maximum epsilon_0 = NBA omega at theta = 90 or 270 degrees.

Converts mechanical to electrical energy. Armature coil rotates in a uniform B; slip rings + brushes connect to external circuit. Commercial: coils stationary, electromagnets rotate. 50 Hz in India, 60 Hz in USA. Capacities up to 500 MW.

front: Motional emf of a rotating rod
back: epsilon = (1/2) B omega R^2, integrating epsilon = integral B v dr over length R with v = omega r. Same via flux through the swept sector: epsilon = B d/dt (1/2 R^2 theta).
